CR_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional client-side severity floor for Cybereason Malops. Accepts info | low | medium | high | critical (plus Cybereason synonyms: informational, important / major, moderate, minor, none / unspecified / unknown). Malops below the floor are dropped from the Faraday output after the per-malop severity normalisation (Cybereason's HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW string severity + the 1-3 numeric malopPriority both bucket onto the Faraday scale). Defaults to info (no filtering).

CR_MALOP_TYPE.description: Optional CSV of Cybereason Malop types to include in the /rest/crimes/unified queryPath. Accepts MalopProcess | MalopLogon | MalopFileless | MalopMobileApp | MalopMobileProcess | MalopMTD plus the legacy MalopMfileWeb / MalopFlash names; unknown / custom types are accepted verbatim and forwarded to the Cybereason API. Blank / unset defaults to the canonical trio (MalopProcess + MalopLogon + MalopFileless) which is what the Cybereason Defense Platform UI queries by default.

name: cybereason
title: Cybereason Defense Platform
description: Cybereason Defense Platform REST importer. Pulls Malops + sensor inventory from a Cybereason on-prem or hosted EDR tenant via POST /rest/crimes/unified (the canonical Malop search the Defense Platform UI uses — queryPath with one entry per Malop type, OVERVIEW templateContext returning the simpleValues / elementValues summary), POST /rest/sensors/query (paginated sensor inventory with limit / offset and a {sensors: [...]} envelope) and POST /rest/visualsearch/query/simple (optional per-malop process evidence search, gated by the CR_INCLUDE_PROCESS_EVIDENCE env so operators can disable the extra round-trips on large tenants where the malop catalogue already carries the rootCauseElements summary). Each Cybereason sensor becomes one Faraday host (ip = the first non-loopback internalIpAddress / externalIpAddress, falling back to synthetic 0.0.0.0 because Cybereason-managed mobile / VDI endpoints often only carry private addresses); Malops attach as Faraday vulnerabilities with engine prefix [EDR]. Severity is bucketed from Cybereason's HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW string severity (plus newer CRITICAL on MTD shapes) and the 1-3 numeric malopPriority (1=low, 2=medium, 3=high), with CVSS bucketing as a fallback. Status mapped from simpleValues.managementStatus (Active -> open, Closed -> closed) + simpleValues.malopStatus (UnderInvestigation / Pending -> open, Remediated / Resolved -> closed, FalsePositive / Muted / Excluded -> risk-accepted). CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from description / detectionType / activityType / decisionFeature simpleValues plus free-form text scans; the Defense Platform rarely surfaces CVEs natively but re-emitted shapes may carry them. Refs include CR-Malop / CR-MalopType / CR-DetectionType / CR-DecisionFeature / CR-RootCause / CR-RootCauseType / CR-Activity pivots, plus MITRE-Tactic / MITRE-Technique pivots when the tenant has the MITRE ATT&CK mapping enabled. Auth: Cybereason uses a session-cookie login flow rooted at POST /login.html (form-encoded username + password); on success the platform returns a JSESSIONID cookie that has to be carried on every /rest/ call. The dispatcher carries the operator's user + password as CR_USER + CR_PASSWORD (a dedicated read-only Cybereason analyst / API user — System -> Users -> add user with the Responder L1 role granted at the global scope is the minimal posture). CR_HOST is the tenant's UI host (e.g. https://acme.cybereason.net for the hosted service or https://defense.acme.corp:8443 for on-prem). Tags: [cybereason, edr, endpoint-edr].
